summary: Chat TTFB degradation following runtime bundle and model ABI rollout for dedicated customer
description:
Issue summary: LayerDocs reports a pronounced increase in time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completion sessions immediately after our 2026-03-13 runtime bundle + model ABI rollout. The regression affects their dedicated pool and started coincident with the rollout window.

Impact: Multiple customer-facing chat flows see median TTFB increase from ~120ms to ~1.2s and tail (95th) up to 3.5s. Customer reports timeouts for long-lived streaming sessions and degraded UX. This customer runs high-throughput interactive assistants; impact is user-visible and revenue-sensitive.

Timeline: 
- 2026-03-13 02:10 UTC: Runtime bundle v1.9.0 deployed to dedicated tenant pools (staged rollout).
- 2026-03-13 02:45 UTC: LayerDocs starts seeing elevated TTFB; support ticket opened by customer's SRE.
- 2026-03-13 03:05 UTC: Rollback of subset of nodes performed for canary; partial mitigation observed for some requests.
- 2026-03-14 09:30 UTC: Support engaged; ticket escalated to infra+serving teams.

Environment: Dedicated GPU pool in us-east, runtime v1.9.0, compiler/ABI bundle 2026-03-13, model pinned to open-redwood-13B-v2 with a customer finetune variant.

Steps to reproduce: 
1) Create chat session using LayerDocs API key pointing to dedicated pool.
2) Send short prompt (~20 tokens) expecting streaming first token within ~150ms.
3) Observe first-token latency logged at client and server traces.

Observed metrics & traces: 
- Elevated median TTFB ~1.2s vs baseline 120ms.
- Service traces show majority of time spent in pre-inference setup: worker assignment, KV-cache restore, and a ~600ms gap on kernel init on ~30% of requests.
- No increase in 5xx rate beyond transient spikes; throughput maintained but higher p95 latency.
- Scheduler logs show increased worker churn around the rollout, with extra warmup cycles.

Logs (not exhaustive): 
- scheduler: node-reassign events at 2026-03-13T02:12:43Z -> multiple rapid rebalancings.
- runtime: kernel_init_duration=0.62s for quant-path on several traces.
- serving: cache_restore_time=0.45s for some sessions.

Hypothesis: The combined bundle included a change to the quantized kernel selection path and a small ABI tweak that introduced a heavier cold-start in the kernel initialization path. For dedicated pools we are seeing worker warmup mismatch: workers are recycled and reinitialized more frequently, causing KV cache and kernel initialization overhead per request. The model ABI change also forces a per-worker compatibility check that adds latency when mixed-version workers are present.

Investigation notes: 
- Reproduced internally with a dedicated dev pool pinned to same runtime+ABI; observed same TTFB increase.
- Rolling a canary rollback to runtime v1.8.7 restored baseline TTFB (~130ms) on canary nodes.
- Quant-path instrumentation suggests a new synchronization barrier introduced in PR runtime#4123 triggers a 500-700ms pause when establishing per-GPU kernel contexts.
- Scheduler team confirmed an aggressive autoscaler reaction during rollout which increased node churn.

Immediate actions taken: 
- Scoped canary rollback to LayerDocs' dedicated pool nodes during business hours (2026-03-13 04:30 UTC) which partially reduced customer-visible TTFB but not fully for sessions that hit recently-initialized workers.
- Feature-flagging the ABI compatibility check in the runtime on LayerDocs pool to test impact.
- Added increased telemetry (kernel_init_duration, cache_restore_time) to traces for next 12 hours.

Next steps / owner assignments: 
- Serving runtime team (assignee: Liam O'Connor) to prepare a hotfix to remove the synchronization barrier in the quant kernel path or optimize it (ETA 2026-03-16).
- Scheduler team to tune autoscaler to avoid simultaneous worker recycle during deploys (owner: Priya Desai, ETA 2026-03-15).
- Release manager to coordinate an opt-in controlled roll-forward once hotfix validated (owner: Anil Kapoor).
- Communicate interim mitigation and ETA to LayerDocs SRE (owner: Sofia Martinez).

Customer communication: We notified LayerDocs SRE on 2026-03-14 10:05 UTC that we identified a likely cause and provided temporary workarounds (rollback and feature-flag). Customer accepted temporary rollback but requested full fix before end of week.

Resolution notes (pending): Hotfix PR opened and under review; scheduler tuning in progress. Will update ticket when hotfix merged and customer verifies restored latency.
